title: Morning Blend v1 — the cup disappeared into the milk.
body:
First proper baseline session for the late-morning cup. Slept around 6.5 hours and woke slightly irritated, mentally cluttered and low-energy because the morning was already fragmented around taking care of my daughter. I wanted to understand what the coffee itself was doing before adding any sensory or functional layers.

The cup felt smooth and soft but almost invisible. Aroma leaned heavily toward warm milk. The coffee itself barely introduced itself. I drank a few sips before breakfast, continued through the meal and finished the remaining cup later. Nothing about the cup demanded attention.

Toward the end I could finally notice a faint woody bitterness underneath the milk structure. That ended up becoming the only memorable moment in the session.

Functionally there was a slight increase in wakefulness and focus, but it was difficult to separate the actual effect of the cup from the excitement of beginning the experiment itself. The session did not fail. It clarified what was missing.
observations: Morning felt rushed and mentally fragmented before the cup
Aroma mostly carried warm milk rather than coffee
Texture smooth but emotionally flat
No strong acidity or bitterness
Slight improvement in wakefulness and focus
The cup lacked identity or memorability
note: The coffee existed physically, but emotionally it disappeared.

title: Morning Blend v2 — the cup finally developed a voice.
body:
Woke around 5AM after roughly six hours of sleep. Managed to get a solid block of focused work done before preparing the session, which changed the emotional starting point entirely compared to yesterday.

Today the cup immediately felt more alive. As I brought it closer, the aroma reminded me of spiced chai, but the sip itself resolved into coffee. That contrast was confusing for a second and then suddenly very interesting.

The drink no longer felt flat. Texture became fuller and warmer. The bitterness integrated into the structure instead of sitting separately. It felt less like an instant coffee and more like an intentional ritual.

Functionally this was the first session where the shift became noticeable. Alertness increased within minutes, sleepiness reduced and mood lifted slightly. The sharper state lasted much longer than yesterday before fading.
observations: Morning started more positively after focused work
Aroma felt familiar like chai, but sip resolved into coffee
Texture fuller and more satisfying than baseline
The cup carried a stronger emotional identity
Alertness sustained much longer than previous day
Sleepiness reduced noticeably
note: For the first time, the drink felt intentional instead of automatic.

title: Morning Blend v3 — warmth replaced sharpness.
body:
Today started very differently. Slept roughly four hours after a difficult night with my daughter and woke around 3:30AM. Despite the sleep deprivation, I still spent a couple of focused hours working before preparing the cup.

I changed too many things at once today and immediately felt the cost of that mistake.

The aroma leaned heavily toward cinnamon from the beginning. The coffee itself became quieter. The cup still felt pleasant, but the emotional direction shifted away from alertness toward comfort.

Instead of feeling ready to move, I felt slower and more grounded. That is not necessarily bad — it is simply wrong for what this SKU is supposed to become.

Another issue emerged near the end of the cup. Spice sediment collected at the bottom and dominated the final sips, which disrupted the finish entirely.
observations: Very sleep-deprived morning before the session
One spice dominated both aroma and emotional direction
Cup became calming instead of activating
Alertness uplift significantly weaker than previous iteration
Final sips carried excessive spice residue
Changing multiple variables together created confusion
note: The cup became emotionally warmer, but lost the edge it needed.

title: Morning Blend v4 — closer to balance, but physically sleepy.
body:
Woke around 5:45AM after roughly six to six-and-a-half hours of sleep. The morning felt calmer than yesterday but less sharp than the strongest earlier session. Spent some relaxed time with my daughter before preparing the cup.

Today the spice felt much more controlled. The aroma entered first through the nose but no longer interrupted the coffee completely. For the first time, the top half of the cup felt directionally balanced.

There was an interesting split in the experience. The beginning of the cup felt cleaner and fresher, while the bottom half slowly drifted back toward spice-heavy territory because residue settled near the end.

Functionally the session created alertness and willingness to work, but physically I still felt sleepy underneath. Even fifteen minutes later while sitting quietly in an AC room, my eyes still wanted to close. The mental shift was clearer than the physical shift.
observations: Fresh preparation softened the spice dominance
Top half of the cup felt more balanced than previous sessions
Residue still disrupted the final sips
Coffee appeared briefly in the middle of the sip
Mental alertness improved more than physical energy
The drink felt closer to its intended direction
note: The mind woke up before the body did.

title: Evening Blend v1 — too many voices inside one cup.
body:
First evening attempt at building a slower conversational drink. The weather outside had turned cold and stormy and the mood naturally leaned inward, which felt like the perfect context for testing this direction.

The first version was chaotic. The cup had richness and weight, but too many flavour systems were competing at once. Spice, bitterness, cacao and coffee all wanted attention simultaneously.

My brother-in-law found it difficult to finish, especially alongside food. The bitterness amplified further with the meal.

I immediately prepared a second variation with a softer structure and that changed the direction completely. The drink became slower, warmer and more cohesive. I personally loved the heavier ritual feeling of it, especially the way it encouraged slower sipping and conversation.
observations: Rainy evening amplified the ritual feeling
First version felt crowded and overly aggressive
Food pairing amplified bitterness heavily
Second variation became much more drinkable
Texture naturally slowed down the pace of drinking
The drink felt closer to a conversation ritual than a coffee
note: This drink was not trying to wake anyone up. It was trying to slow the room down.

title: Evening Blend v2 — the room finally slowed down.
body:
Second evening iteration using the same tester as reference. This mattered because now I could observe progression instead of isolated reactions.

The cup immediately felt calmer and more balanced than yesterday. The bitterness softened. Warmth increased. Thickness now felt intentional rather than excessive.

One guest described the drink as reminding him of a traditional ritual tonic, while another noticed a nutty dessert-like warmth in the aroma. Both reactions were useful.

Most importantly, nobody rushed through the cup. The drink naturally slowed the pace of the room. Conversation stretched longer without the drink demanding attention constantly.
observations: Bitterness reduced significantly from previous night
Warmth and texture became more cohesive
Guests naturally slowed their drinking pace
The cup encouraged longer conversation windows
The emotional territory became clearer
More memorable than traditional instant coffee
note: The drink stopped interrupting the conversation and started accompanying it.

title: Evening Blend v3 — less medicinal, more conversational.
body:
Third evening iteration with returning testers. The atmosphere was rushed because they only had a few minutes before leaving for somewhere, which made the feedback less reflective and more instinctive.

That actually helped.

The immediate response was that the drink felt easier and less bitter than previous versions. The spice layers no longer dominated the cup aggressively.

One interesting thing: the earlier comparison to a medicinal tonic did not return this time. That suggests the drink is slowly moving away from 'functional concoction' territory and closer toward an actual evening ritual beverage.

The thickness now felt aligned with the purpose of the drink rather than accidental.
observations: Short tasting window created instinctive reactions
Guests found it easier to drink than earlier versions
Bitterness no longer became the dominant memory
Spices moved into the background instead of leading
Texture now felt intentional
Conversation around the drink became calmer and more curious
note: The drink is slowly moving from experimentation toward ritual.

title: Evening Blend v4 — cleaner mechanics, weaker identity.
body:
Tonight's session was prepared more carefully to solve the sediment and unevenness issues from previous iterations. The cup became technically cleaner, but emotionally less distinct.

The aroma leaned strongly toward one warm spice again, while the coffee itself almost disappeared. My wife immediately associated the aroma with kahwa rather than coffee.

The texture became lighter than previous versions and the cup visually resembled a spiced herbal drink in the glass. Bitterness from the cacao stayed present while the emotional warmth reduced.

Instead of encouraging conversation naturally, the session became more analytical. I kept evaluating the drink while drinking it. That itself felt like a signal that the emotional direction is still unresolved.
observations: Cleaner preparation removed sediment problems
Coffee identity weakened further behind spice and cacao
The cup visually resembled kahwa in a glass cup
Bitterness remained while emotional warmth reduced
The drink became easier to analyse than enjoy
Important lesson around identity versus technical smoothness
note: Cleaning up the mechanics exposed that the emotional identity itself is still unresolved.

title: Morning Blend v5 — cardamom delivery method changed.
body:
Used freshly crushed inner seeds instead of pre-ground powder, reduced the quantity slightly compared to earlier versions. The rest of the structure remained mostly stable.

Compared to the second iteration, this cup felt much more balanced. The spice no longer overpowered the coffee immediately. The aroma still entered through the spice first, but by the time I actually tasted the sip, the coffee came through more naturally.

There was an interesting sensory transition: the spice arrived through the nose first, coffee through the mouth later. That duality felt more intentional today.

Toward the second half and especially the final sip, the spice started becoming stronger again. Visible fine residue settled at the bottom, which likely caused the later sips to become more spice-heavy than the earlier ones. The top half and bottom half of the cup almost behaved like slightly different drinks.

Functionally the session created alertness and improved mental orientation, but not physical activation. Sitting idle in an AC room afterward, my eyes were still closing. The cup appears to improve cognitive readiness more than bodily energy.
observations: Fresh-crushed seeds instead of powder — cleaner aroma integration
Spice arrived through nose, coffee through mouth — improved sequence
Top half balanced, bottom half spice-heavy from residue
Mental alertness improved, physical activation less clear
Residue problem persists but appeared later in the cup
Delivery method more important than quantity alone
note: The flavour direction is close. The structural problem is delivery and distribution, not the ingredient itself.

title: Evening Blend v5 — cardamom infusion method tested.
body:
Attempted to solve the cardamom residue problem through infusion rather than direct dissolution. Cracked the seeds, steeped them in the hot water for a minute, then strained before adding the dry ingredients.

The infusion solved the residue and unevenness problem. The cup was technically cleaner than any previous version — no sediment, no spice-heavy final sips, consistent experience throughout.

But: the cardamom almost disappeared. My wife could not detect it at all from a distance. The cup no longer felt distinctive. It tasted like a smooth, slightly flat drink with very mild bitterness and a slightly thicker body — but the identity collapsed.

Straining had solved the mechanics but removed the aromatic personality. The volatile oils that create the top note and the surprise contrast seem to evaporate during the steeping and straining process.

Key realisation: the infusion method solves residue but erases the sensory signature. A cleaner cup that nobody notices is worse than a slightly imperfect cup that people remember.
observations: Infusion method: steeped and strained before adding other ingredients
Zero sediment — technically the cleanest cup yet
Cardamom aroma almost completely absent
Wife could not detect any spice from distance
Cinnamon dominated what little aroma remained
Cup felt generic — no intrigue, no mystery
note: Solved the mechanics. Erased the personality. Technical cleanliness without emotional identity is worse than the original problem.

title: Morning Blend v6 — coffee base switched, rhodiola introduced.
body:
First session with a different instant coffee base — switched from the familiar South Indian blend to a Colombian single-origin instant. Also introduced a measured amount of rhodiola powder, opening the capsule directly into the cup.

Aroma was slightly better than yesterday — there was a slight lingering top note but nothing assertive. A somewhat pungent smell appeared which I initially could not place. On reflection this was likely the rhodiola itself, which has a characteristic earthy-herbal note in raw powder form.

The taste was stronger than previous sessions. Something bitter was consistently present throughout — again, likely the rhodiola interacting with the milk rather than fully dissolving. The cup wall showed fine residue after drinking, consistent with undissolved functional powder.

The functional state shift was present but modest on a reasonable baseline day. Alertness moved by approximately one point, focus similarly. Energy was unchanged. The rhodiola's anti-fatigue mechanism requires a fatigued baseline to show its full effect — a good-baseline day underestimates it.
observations: Colombian instant base: sharper and more acidic than previous South Indian blend
Rhodiola powder introduced: characteristic pungent note detected
Cup wall residue from functional powder — dissolution problem identified
Bitter aftertaste not from coffee — likely functional ingredient
50:50 water-milk ratio maintained — balance improved
Functional shift modest on good baseline — expected
note: The functional ingredient introduced a taste and dissolution problem. Format needs to change before the cup can be served to others.

title: Evening Blend v6 — simplification breakthrough. Wife says: alcoholic.
body:
Removed cinnamon entirely. Removed black pepper entirely. Switched to Dutch-processed cocoa powder instead of raw cacao. Switched coffee base to a cleaner Colombian instant. Kept: cocoa, coconut jaggery, and a very small amount of nutmeg.

This was the most significant reset of the evening blend so far.

My wife smelled it before tasting and said: it smells like an alcoholic drink. She could not place it anywhere. When she tasted it, she said it reminded her of nothing she had drunk before — not kadha, not hot chocolate, not café mocha.

This is the target state. The cup is no longer identifiable as a spiced coffee or a wellness drink. It exists in its own unclassified territory. The aroma produces social curiosity. The taste grounds rather than stimulates. The experience creates conversation without demanding explanation.

The kadha association is completely gone. This is the breakthrough session the evening blend needed.
observations: All warm spices removed except one at micro-dose
Dutch-processed cocoa: smoother, less bitter, dissolves better than raw cacao
Wife could not categorise the drink from smell alone
Wife said: it smells like an alcoholic drink
No kadha association — this is gone for the first time
Thickness slightly less than previous versions — needs addressing
note: Wife said it smells like an alcoholic drink and could not place it anywhere she had tasted before. The kadha association is gone.

title: Morning Blend v7 — Colombian confirmed. Rhodiola format problem.
body:
Ran a clean comparison between the Colombian and South Indian blend bases in separate cups, then confirmed Colombian as the morning base. Colombian reads as sharper, slightly acidic, with an unidentifiable character note that makes it more interesting than the South Indian blend in this context.

Rhodiola powder format confirmed as a problem for the sachet. The raw powder does not dissolve cleanly in a water-milk mixture. The fat in the milk creates a barrier around the particles, which explains the cup-wall residue and the bitter concentrated final sips. The format needs to change — either water-soluble extract or a functional alternative.

L-theanine tested as a rhodiola substitute. It dissolves completely, contributes no taste, and produces the alpha-wave smoothing effect that reduces caffeine jitter without dulling alertness. Not identical to rhodiola's anti-fatigue mechanism but practically useful and sachet-compatible.
observations: Colombian vs South Indian blind comparison: Colombian clearly more interesting
Colombian: sharp, acidic, distinctive unnamed note — right direction
Rhodiola raw powder: cup wall residue confirmed — format problem
L-theanine substitute tested: clean dissolution, no taste impact
L-theanine effect: smoother alertness curve, less friction entering work
Cardamom quantity needs increase — present but too quiet
note: Colombian is the base. Rhodiola format is wrong. L-theanine is the bridge until water-soluble extract is sourced.

title: Morning Blend v8 — Blue Tokai medium-dark microground introduced.
body:
Visited the local Blue Tokai outlet and obtained their Baarbara Estate at medium-dark roast, ground at Turkish fineness. This is the first session using fresh-ground specialty coffee as part of the morning blend.

The difference in aroma was immediate and unmistakable. When hot water hit the microground, a roasted warmth lifted into the steam that the instant format had never produced. The cup smelled intentional before the first sip.

The blend combined the fresh-ground base with a small amount of instant for solubility, plus the confirmed spice and functional stack.

The spice arrived as the top note and receded naturally during the middle of the cup. Coffee identity was clearer than in any previous morning iteration. The functional shift was cleaner than the rhodiola powder sessions — less bitter residue, smoother alertness curve.

The residue problem from the microground remained in the final sips, but at this grind level it was significantly reduced and felt like a texture note rather than a concentrated spice dump.
observations: Fresh-ground medium-dark at Turkish fineness: roasted warmth immediately present in steam
Aroma distinction from instant base was immediately noticeable
Hybrid format: microground for aroma + instant for solubility
Spice arrived as top note, receded naturally — correct sequence
Coffee identity clearer than any previous morning session
Microground sediment in final sips: tolerable at this grind level
note: The aroma problem is solved. The cup now smells like something worth paying attention to before the first sip.

title: Evening Blend v7 — mace introduced. The mystery deepens.
body:
Replaced the previous micro-spice with mace powder at a very small quantity. Mace is the outer lacy covering of the nutmeg seed — more delicate and floral than nutmeg, and at low doses nearly unidentifiable.

The aroma from the steam was immediately different from previous versions. Something warm and slightly ethereal that nobody in the room could name. Brother-in-law smelled it and said: what is that? He guessed several things — none of them correct.

Added mulethi for the first time as a base note. The lingering sweetness on the back of the tongue extended the finish significantly. Ten minutes after finishing the cup, the palate still carried a faint pleasant warmth.

The cup is now producing the full emotional arc: intrigue on the nose before the first sip, warmth and depth through the middle, and a lingering sweetness that stays after the cup is gone. Brother-in-law finished the entire cup without pausing.
observations: Mace at micro-dose: warm, floral, completely unidentifiable to tester
Brother-in-law: what is that? — could not guess the ingredient
Mulethi introduced as base note: trailing natural sweetness
Finish extended noticeably — palate warmth present 10 minutes after
Brother-in-law completed the entire cup without pausing
No bitter aftertaste — mulethi replaced bitterness with sweetness
note: The three-layer emotional arc is working. Top note creates intrigue. Middle creates warmth. Base note creates the reason to linger.

title: Morning Blend v9 — rhodiola replaced with L-theanine. Stack locked.
body:
Final functional stack configuration tested. Replaced rhodiola powder entirely with L-theanine for the sachet format. The decision is pragmatic and correct: L-theanine dissolves completely, contributes no taste, and produces a meaningfully smoother alertness curve that most people will notice within one session.

The cup was clean from start to finish. No residue, no bitter aftertaste, no cup-wall cling. The spice top note arrived correctly and receded by mid-cup. The coffee identity from the microground base held throughout.

Functional shift at 45 minutes: noticeably smoother cognitive engagement. The difference from caffeine-only sessions is the absence of the mid-morning jitter and the extension of the focused window. Not more energy — better-quality energy.

This is the locked morning blend. The sachet format works. The preparation is single-step. The experience is clean, distinctive, and functionally real.
observations: L-theanine: complete dissolution, zero taste impact, zero residue
Single-step preparation confirmed: all ingredients dissolve cleanly together
Spice top note correct: arrives first, recedes mid-cup
Functional shift at 45 min: smoother alertness, reduced cognitive friction
No bitter aftertaste — cleanest finish of all morning sessions
Ready for Layer 1 external testing
note: This is the locked morning blend. Single-step, clean, functional, and distinctive enough to serve to someone who did not know what was coming.

title: Kisse v1 — mystery survives, comfort does not.
body:
Tonight's cup confirmed something important. The drink is beginning to occupy its own territory. It no longer feels like coffee, chai, hot chocolate or kadha. It sits somewhere between them. The problem is that being different is not automatically valuable.

The aroma generated curiosity but the experience itself felt thinner than expected. The drink invited analysis more than attachment. I found myself thinking about the ingredients instead of relaxing into the cup.

For the first time, the distinction between mystery and comfort became visible. The cup could create intrigue without creating emotional warmth.
observations: Cup feels increasingly difficult to classify
Curiosity generated before first sip
Body thinner than expected
Comfort level lower than intrigue level
Drink encourages analysis
Beginning of mystery versus comfort split
note: Being interesting is not the same as being comforting.

title: Fresh-ground El Diablo enters the project.
body:
Today was the first serious move away from instant coffee thinking. Fresh-ground El Diablo changed the ritual before the first sip even happened.

When hot water touched the grounds, the room smelled different. The cup suddenly had anticipation. Aroma became part of the experience rather than decoration.

This session created a new question. If aroma changes the emotional state before tasting, perhaps coffee is not simply a carrier ingredient. Perhaps aroma itself is part of the state shift.
observations: Fresh grinding dramatically improved aroma
Anticipation appeared before first sip
Coffee felt premium and intentional
Instant coffee limitations became obvious
Aroma started becoming part of the ritual
Fresh-ground direction validated
note: The smell arriving before the sip changed everything.

title: The best cup appears — and refuses to repeat.
body:
One evening session finally delivered something special. The aroma carried dark chocolate and unusual barrel-like notes. My wife described it as slightly alcoholic, almost whiskey-like, despite there being no alcohol present.

The cup felt smooth, integrated and memorable. For a brief moment it felt like the drink had found its identity.

The frustration arrived later. Subsequent attempts using nearly identical ingredients failed to recreate the same result. The breakthrough was real, but the mechanism behind it remained unclear.
observations: Dark chocolate aroma emerged naturally
Whiskey-like notes observed
Cup felt integrated and complete
Wife preferred this version
Recipe could not be replicated consistently
Breakthrough without repeatability
note: The best cup so far appeared by accident and disappeared just as quickly.

title: El Diablo versus Monsoon Malabar.
body:
Ran a direct comparison between freshly ground El Diablo and Monsoon Malabar using identical preparation methods.

El Diablo felt sharper, cleaner and more expressive. Sweetness was easier to notice and the finish remained clearer.

Monsoon Malabar felt earthy, muted and slightly muddy. It was not unpleasant but lacked the lift and complexity that El Diablo brought.

The comparison confirmed that coffee is shaping the emotional profile of the drink more than originally expected.
observations: El Diablo cleaner and more expressive
Monsoon Malabar earthier and flatter
Sweetness easier to notice in El Diablo
Coffee influences overall emotional profile
Bean selection matters
El Diablo remains reference bean
note: Coffee is becoming a character, not a background ingredient.

title: Customer interviews reveal two different drinks.
body:
Survey responses started creating an unexpected pattern.

Some people were drawn toward the dark, mysterious, conversation-led version. Others responded strongly to entirely different language: rainy evenings, reading, cocoon-like comfort, slowing down and being alone with their thoughts.

This was not a recipe insight. It was a positioning insight.

The possibility emerged that one drink might be trying to satisfy two emotional jobs simultaneously.
observations: Comfort language repeated frequently
Rainy evenings appeared multiple times
Reading and personal rituals mentioned often
Mystery still generated curiosity
Two emotional territories identified
Potential SKU split emerging
note: The next question may not be culinary. It may be emotional.

title: Coconut milk powder solves one problem and creates another.
body:
Introduced coconut milk powder to improve body and richness.

The improvement was immediate. The cup felt fuller and smoother. Sweetness became more integrated and the drink moved slightly closer to the comforting direction suggested by survey responses.

Unfortunately the surface developed visible particles and residue collected on the cup walls. The cup tasted better while looking worse.

This was the first time presentation became a major concern.
observations: Body improved noticeably
Smoothness increased
Sweetness integrated better
Visible surface particles appeared
Residue remained on cup walls
Taste improved faster than presentation
note: A better drink is not automatically a better product.

title: The recurring complaint: uncooked, powdery, lukewarm.
body:
Multiple tasting sessions with family revealed a remarkably consistent pattern.

Nobody complained about sweetness. Nobody complained about bitterness. Coffee was present. Cacao was present.

Instead, three complaints repeated over and over: powdery texture, residue on the glass and a cup that arrived lukewarm rather than comforting.

The insight was important because it suggested the biggest barriers may be operational rather than flavour related.
observations: Sweetness generally accepted
Bitterness generally acceptable
Powdery texture repeatedly mentioned
Cup wall residue repeatedly mentioned
Temperature consistently too low
Operational problems masking recipe quality
note: Nobody remembers the flavour if the cup arrives cold.

title: The real problem may be wow, not flavour.
body:
Tonight's reflection moved beyond ingredients.

The drink is now reasonably drinkable. Coffee is present. Cacao is present. Sweetness is balanced. Yet something still feels missing.

The question is no longer whether the cup works. The question is whether it creates a feeling someone would remember.

Current hypothesis: Kisse is caught between two identities. One wants to be a mysterious conversation drink. The other wants to be a comforting personal ritual. Both directions have supporters. Neither has fully arrived.

The next phase of development will focus less on flavour correction and more on emotional clarity.
observations: Drinkability improving
Identity still unresolved
Mystery direction has supporters
Comfort direction has supporters
No clear wow moment yet
Emotional clarity becoming the primary challenge
note: The next breakthrough will likely come from choosing an emotion, not an ingredient.

title: Morning Blend v10 — Mokka Farms 80-20 enters the recipe.
body:
First session with Mokka Farms 80-20 Arabica-Robusta at moka-pot grind replacing Colombian instant. Tested whether the Robusta component would add crema-like body and sharper roasted note.

The cup was immediately more assertive than previous iterations. Something about the Robusta added a coffee-forward character that Colombian did not. Cardamom arrived in the first few sips rather than collecting at the bottom.

However the milk ratio at 35ml was too high — aroma collapsed completely after adding milk. Everything went flat. The lesson learned today: aroma is not surviving high milk ratios regardless of which coffee base is used.
observations: Mokka Farms 80-20 moka-pot grind at 0.9g — assertive, sharp roasted note
Colombian replaced — cleaner experiment isolation
Cardamom arriving in first sips for first time — correct distribution
35ml milk destroyed aroma completely — ratio confirmed as wrong
Jaggery stevia-like at low concentration — needs stronger coffee base to contextualise
Sediment at setting 10 confirmed acceptable
note: The milk ratio is killing the aroma. 30ml maximum, not 35ml.

title: Evening Blend v9 — worst iteration. Mace at 3-4 pinches is too much.
body:
Prepared KISSE at 9:30pm for guests at home. Used Monsoon Malabar moka-pot grind, Levista, Dutch cocoa, coconut jaggery, a pinch of cinnamon, 3-4 pinches of mace. 80ml water, 30ml milk.

Immediately wrong. Mace at this quantity is resinous and medicinal — it stops being mysterious and becomes a dominant herbal note. The aroma before adding milk was 'Indian masala soup'. Cinnamon was immediately identifiable by my wife.

All spice, no coffee. The drink existed in the wrong emotional territory entirely. This session confirmed two permanent decisions: cinnamon is permanently removed from KISSE, and mace must be measured at 0.05g or less — not pinches.
observations: 3-4 pinches of mace — catastrophically too much
Aroma read as masala soup rather than mysterious warmth
Wife immediately identified cinnamon — kills mystery
Cinnamon permanently removed from KISSE from this session forward
Mace quantity must be measured on scale — no more pinches
Drink entirely in wrong emotional territory
note: Cinnamon removed permanently. Mace must be 0.05g on scale, not a pinch.

title: Morning Blend v11 — grind comparison test. Malabar moka vs Jack Daniels medium.
body:
Ran the grind format comparison test with two half-cups of RUKH. Cup A: Monsoon Malabar at moka-pot grind setting. Cup B: Jack Daniels Tennessee Whiskey Coffee pre-ground (medium grind).

Evaluation focused on three things: aroma in first 10 seconds, sediment in final sips, grittiness on palate.

Malabar moka-pot grind: finer particles, better distributed aroma, particles settled cleanly rather than floating. Jack Daniels medium grind: visibly larger particles floating on surface, gritty mouthfeel throughout, did not integrate into liquid.

Moka-pot grind confirmed as the correct format for RUKH microground component. Jack Daniels medium grind eliminated. The Jack Daniels flavour profile itself is interesting for KISSE due to barrel character, but the grind format is wrong for direct dissolution.
observations: Malabar moka-pot: finer particles, better aroma release, clean settling
Jack Daniels medium: floating particles, gritty mouthfeel, wrong format
Moka-pot grind confirmed as correct format for all SKUs
Jack Daniels whiskey barrel character noted — worth testing for KISSE specifically
Aroma comparison: Malabar earthier, JD smokier — both have character
Decision: one unified grind level, moka-pot fineness, across all SKUs
note: Grind format closed. Moka-pot fineness confirmed for all specialty coffee components.

title: Evening Blend v10 — El Diablo enters the project. Setting 10.
body:
Third Wave Coffee El Diablo whole bean arrived. First grinding session with AAshonee grinder at setting 10. Freshly ground El Diablo at 2.2g combined with Levista 0.7g, Dutch cocoa 1.0g, palm jaggery 2.0g, mace at 0.05g knife tip, vanilla 4 drops.

The aroma from freshly ground El Diablo was immediately different from anything tested previously. A café-like roasted warmth came from the first stir. My wife smelled it before tasting and said it was more complex than previous iterations.

Sediment at setting 10 settled cleanly into the bottom by the final sips and did not come into the mouth during normal drinking. Grinder confirmed as working correctly at this setting for KISSE format.
observations: El Diablo at setting 10 — café-like aroma immediately present
Wife noted more complexity than previous KISSE iterations
Sediment settled cleanly — setting 10 confirmed for KISSE
Mace at knife tip: detectable warmth, not identifiable as a named spice
Vanilla at 4 drops: warmth present in chest 8 minutes after last sip
Dutch cocoa at 1.0g: chocolate depth present without hot chocolate direction
note: El Diablo changes everything. The café aroma was missing from every previous session. This is the right bean.

title: Evening Blend v11 — three guests. First external KISSE test.
body:
Made three cups of KISSE for wife, brother-in-law, and one guest at 10:30pm. Recipe: El Diablo setting 10 at 2.2g, Levista 0.7g, Dutch cocoa 1.0g, palm jaggery 2.0g, mace knife tip, vanilla 4 drops, 110ml water, 25ml warm milk.

Guest who does not normally drink black coffee: tried it with some reluctance after encouragement. Said 'edible and different'. Did not ask for milk after the first sip despite his prior stated preference.

Wife: better than morning but not as good as the breakthrough session from two days ago. Could sense coffee and slight cocoa. No specific complaint about ingredients.

Brother-in-law: could taste coffee but could not identify other ingredients. Found it thinner than espresso which he prefers.

Three external data points. All finished the cup. Nobody identified mace or vanilla specifically.
observations: Guest who avoids black coffee finished entire cup — significant signal
Guest said 'edible and different' — no named ingredient detected
Wife: better than previous but not as good as El Diablo breakthrough session
Brother-in-law: coffee present, other ingredients unidentifiable — correct state
All three finished cups — first time this has happened with external testers
Thickness complaint from espresso-drinker — coconut milk powder needed
note: All three external testers finished their cups. The cup is working. The format is not yet commercial-ready.

title: Morning Blend v12 — RUKH with Baarbara setting 10. Aroma gap solved.
body:
First RUKH session with Blue Tokai Baarbara Estate medium-dark whole bean, ground at setting 10 on AAshonee grinder. Recipe: Baarbara 0.9g, Cothas Royal 1.8g, Toffee Colombian 0.7g, cardamom 0.14g, coconut jaggery 1.5g dry before water, L-theanine 200mg, orange peel powder 0.06g, cinnamon 0.08g. 90ml water, 30ml warm milk.

When hot water hit the Baarbara microground, a roasted warmth came from the steam that had not been present in any previous RUKH session. The aroma problem that had existed for four weeks was solved in one session.

Functional state shift at 45 minutes: noticeably smoother alertness curve. No jitter. Focus improved without anxiety. The L-theanine is doing what it should.

Cardamom arrived as top note in first sips. Orange peel added a citrus lift that nobody could immediately identify. This is the RUKH identity.
observations: Baarbara microground: roasted warmth in steam — aroma problem solved
Orange peel 0.06g: sharp citrus lift, unidentifiable as orange
Cardamom as top note in first sips — correct sequence achieved
L-theanine: smooth alertness curve, no jitter at 45 minutes
Coconut jaggery added dry before water — integrates fully
This is the closest RUKH has been to its intended emotional character
note: Baarbara solved the aroma gap. The cup now smells like something worth paying attention to. RUKH is directionally locked.

title: Evening Blend v12 — steep and strain method discovered.
body:
Changed the entire preparation method for KISSE. Instead of dissolving El Diablo directly, steeped 3g at setting 17 in 100ml hot water for 4 minutes covered, then strained into the cacao-jaggery-mace paste.

When I removed the plate after 4 minutes, the aroma that came from the cup was genuinely café-like. The first time any KISSE session has produced this. My wife said: whiskey and dark chocolate. She could identify both elements separately and said it was the best version yet.

The steep and strain method extracts properly rather than dissolving. Four minutes at setting 17 is the confirmed method for KISSE going forward.
observations: Steep and strain method: properly extracts rather than dissolves
Setting 17 for 4 minutes covered — correct extraction parameters
Aroma on removing cover: café-like, genuinely complex
Wife said: whiskey and dark chocolate — first time two distinct notes detected
Wife confirmed: best KISSE iteration yet
Preparation method is now confirmed — this is how KISSE is made
note: Wife said whiskey and dark chocolate. This is the preparation method. Steep and strain at setting 17 for 4 minutes.

title: Evening Blend v13 — Monsoon Malabar vs El Diablo steep and strain.
body:
Comparison session: same steep and strain method, same recipe, same everything — only the bean changed. Cup A: El Diablo setting 17. Cup B: Monsoon Malabar moka-pot grind.

El Diablo: complex, slightly sweet finish, whiskey character, chocolate depth. Held attention throughout.

Monsoon Malabar: muddy, earthy, flat, no distinctive finish. The earthiness that works in a morning format becomes an obstacle in the evening warmth context.

Decision confirmed: El Diablo is KISSE's bean. Monsoon Malabar goes to RUKH testing only and even there it is not the right direction.
observations: El Diablo: complex, sweet, whiskey-chocolate — clear winner
Monsoon Malabar: muddy, earthy, flat — wrong for KISSE
Bean comparison closed: El Diablo confirmed for KISSE
Malabar's earthiness works in morning format, not evening
Method identical — only bean changed — clean comparison
El Diablo also has better finish and aftertaste than Malabar
note: El Diablo confirmed. Bean decision closed. Do not reopen this.

title: Morning Blend v13 — RUKH second Baarbara session. Recipe near-lock.
body:
Second clean RUKH session with Baarbara. Held all variables identical to previous session. The cup reproduced almost exactly — cardamom top note, orange peel citrus lift, roasted Baarbara warmth underneath.

Functional state shift at 45 minutes confirmed again. Smooth alertness, reduced cognitive friction, no jitter. L-theanine is consistently working.

This is the second consecutive session producing the same result. RUKH is ready for sachet format testing. Recipe considered locked pending sachet simulation.
observations: Second consecutive identical RUKH session — reproducibility confirmed
Cardamom top note: arriving first and receding naturally mid-cup
Orange peel: sharp citrus lift, unidentifiable as orange
Baarbara roasted depth: present throughout, sustains into final sips
L-theanine 200mg: smooth alertness at 45 minutes confirmed again
Ready for sachet format simulation
note: Same cup twice in a row. This is what locked looks like. RUKH is ready.

title: Evening Blend v14 — user research changes the brief. Cocoon direction found.
body:
Received survey responses from five external respondents on Option A versus Option B positioning.

Most important response: one respondent described Option A as 'quiet catharsis — cocoon-like comfort, a small pause where you just feel yourself.' She said she would buy regularly and pay Rs 50-75. Her current evening drink is regular coffee or tea.

This response reframed the entire KISSE brief. The product is not a mysterious social drink. It is a personal pause ritual. The emotional brief is now: a quiet cup for your own company.

Rs 50 validated by four of five respondents. Option B has broader daily use but Option A has deeper emotional resonance for self-comfort moments. Direction confirmed: Option A, cocoon comfort.
observations: 50-50 split on Option A versus Option B overall
Option B stronger for daily use, Option A stronger for emotional resonance
Rs 50 per sachet confirmed by four of five respondents
Key customer insight: quiet catharsis, cocoon comfort, personal pause
Evening drink currently: tea or herbal tea for all respondents
KISSE positioning: not social ritual, personal pause
note: She said: a small pause where you just feel yourself. That is the product brief.

title: Evening Blend v15 — three-way comparison. Raw cacao eliminated permanently.
body:
Ran three parallel half-cups to isolate ingredient contributions. Control: El Diablo plus Dutch cocoa plus coconut milk powder. Cup B: El Diablo plus Dutch cocoa only. Cup C: El Diablo plus raw cacao powder.

Raw cacao in Cup C: earthy, algae-like, grainy texture on the palate. Wrong for sachet format — will not dissolve without blooming step the end user cannot perform.

Dutch cocoa in Cup B: clean, no surface issues, acceptable body.

Control with coconut milk powder: smoothest taste but visible particles on surface from generic roller-dried brand.

Decision: raw cacao eliminated permanently from KISSE. Dutch cocoa confirmed. Nestlé or Kara spray-dried coconut milk powder needed to solve surface particle problem.
observations: Raw cacao: earthy algae note, grainy, undissolved particles — eliminated
Dutch cocoa: clean dissolution, acceptable body, no surface issues
Coconut milk powder: smoothest taste but visible surface particles from wrong brand
Generic roller-dried coconut milk powder inadequate — spray-dried needed
Raw cacao eliminated permanently from KISSE
Dutch cocoa confirmed as final cacao component
note: Raw cacao eliminated. Dutch cocoa confirmed. One decision made.

title: Evening Blend v16 — first external guest tasting. 'Different. Is it tea and coffee?'
body:
Served KISSE to one external guest at home. Recipe: El Diablo steep and strain setting 17, Dutch cocoa, palm jaggery, mace, vanilla, cinnamon at end. Guest tasted blind without explanation.

First comment: it's different. Is it a mixture of tea and coffee?

Guest left half finished. Cinnamon was detectable and he asked about it. He said do not remove cinnamon but there is some other masala in the coffee.

Two key findings: cinnamon permanently confirmed as wrong — any quantity is identifiable and disrupts mystery. Guest leaving half finished is the hardest data point received. The cup is not yet good enough to serve commercially.

The 'different' reaction is correct positioning. The half-finished cup is the honest verdict on the current version.
observations: Guest said: it's different, is it a mixture of tea and coffee
Guest left half finished — hard signal that current version insufficient
Cinnamon immediately detectable — permanently confirmed as wrong for KISSE
Guest could sense masala — mace quantity or preparation still creating herbal note
No milk used in this session — cup was not hot enough
Temperature consistently identified as problem across all sessions
note: Guest left half finished. The product is not ready yet. This is the honest data.

title: Evening Blend v17 — three external testers. Sachet format simulation.
body:
Made three cups of KISSE for wife, father-in-law, and one guest using sachet simulation format. Two cups prepared via steep and strain separately, one cup with all dry ingredients combined.

Three consistent feedbacks received: powdery feel from undissolved ingredients, visible sediment on cup walls, and cups not hot enough — all three found the drink lukewarm.

Father-in-law said taste is good. Guest said edible and different — same as previous external session. Wife gave more detailed feedback later.

The preparation format is creating three specific operational problems. None are recipe problems. All are solvable: spray-dried coconut milk powder, boiling water poured immediately, fine mesh strainer.
observations: Three external testers — all found cup lukewarm
Powdery texture from undissolved cocoa and coconut milk powder
Visible wall residue from particles
Father-in-law: taste is good — positive baseline from non-coffee drinker
Guest repeated: edible and different — no ingredient identified
All three problems operational not recipe — solvable without new ingredients
note: The recipe is working. The preparation format needs three operational fixes before external sachets can go out.

title: Evening Blend v18 — cocoon recipe formulated. Awaiting spray-dried coconut milk.
body:
Reformulated KISSE entirely around the cocoon emotional brief from user research.

Three specific changes from previous recipe: coconut milk powder increased to 3.0g with Nestlé or Kara spray-dried brand required, vanilla bean powder increased to 0.3g for persistent warmth aroma through the entire steep, palm jaggery increased to 2.8g for gentle comfort sweetness. Coffee reduced to 2.5g to remove sharpness that works against the cocoon feeling.

The cocoon architecture is designed around: fat from coconut milk providing mouthfeel and coating sensation, vanilla at meaningful dose creating sustained warmth throughout the cup, jaggery at slightly higher level providing gentle emotional comfort not dessert sweetness.

The session could not be fully executed today because spray-dried coconut milk powder has not arrived. Nestlé or Kara brand required — generic roller-dried brands create surface particles confirmed across multiple sessions.
observations: Cocoon emotional brief confirmed from user research
Coffee reduced to 2.5g — softness over sharpness for evening
Vanilla doubled to 0.3g — persistent warmth architecture
Coconut milk powder at 3.0g — fat required for mouthfeel
Awaiting Nestlé or Kara spray-dried brand
Preparation ritual reframed: do nothing else for 4 minutes
note: The recipe is ready. The ingredient is not. Tomorrow is the first real cocoon session.
